name: MS-01
label: Safe R

key_factors: District leans Republican by roughly 18 points and the national environment favors the GOP this cycle
Incumbent Trent Kelly holds a large money advantage, about $860,000 on hand versus $150,000 for Cliff Johnson
No competitive polling exists and prediction markets price the Republican around 95 percent
model.rationale: The district's deep Republican lean, Kelly's incumbency and financial edge, and a favorable national environment all point the same direction, and markets price this at roughly 95 percent Republican. Johnson's modest fundraising gives no evidence of the resources needed to close an 18-point structural gap.
model.watch: A late wave of outside spending against Kelly or credible polling showing a single-digit race would be the first sign this is moving toward competitive.
notes: No expert rater lists this race; treated as safe for the party holding the seat.
No usable general-election polls; forecast rests on fundamentals and expert ratings.

overview:
Mississippi's 1st District, anchored in the state's northeast, leans about 18 points toward Republicans, and Representative Trent Kelly is seeking another term with the advantages of incumbency. He has raised just over $1 million and holds roughly $860,000 on hand, well ahead of Democratic challenger Cliff Johnson, who has raised about $550,000 with $150,000 remaining. A Libertarian candidate is also on the ballot.

No public general-election polls are available, and no major expert raters have flagged the race as competitive. Prediction markets put the Republican's chances around 95 percent. With the district's strong lean and a national environment that favors Republicans this year, the race is rated Safe Republican, with Kelly expected to win by roughly 17 points. Johnson would need an unusually large electoral shift to make this contest close.
